subject: Private deployment: vault handoff & tenant gateway data boundaries
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@arborbio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Diaz <legal@arborbio.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — KMS responsibilities & handoff questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're generally positive about moving ahead with a Private (VPC) deployment, but our security team needs clarification on three items before we proceed to contracting:

1) Customer-controlled keys: ArborBio requires that the master encryption keys for all customer data be strictly customer-managed (BYOK in a KMS/HSM controlled by us). Please confirm whether Redwood will: 1) accept customer-managed keys only, 2) ever possess plaintext key material, and 3) support HSM-based access policies (e.g., allowlist specific Redwood service principals).

2) Operator access & breakglass: We need a documented, auditable operator access model — for example, an operator jump-host in our VPC that allows session recording and one-time breakglass keys. Please outline Redwood's proposed operational access flow and whether you can limit operator actions to non-plaintext, read-only logs and diagnostics unless breakglass is approved.

3) Data egress / subprocessors: We need an explicit list of subprocessors that will have any ability to process or see customer data in the private deployment (including monitoring agents, metrics collectors, and third-party log storage). Also confirm whether any telemetry or crash dumps might be routed outside our VPC (and if so, how they're encrypted/retained).

Attached is a short network diagram our infra team suggested — it highlights the demarcation we expect. Can your legal/ops teams review and send a DPA addendum tailored to private deployments? We can move quickly if we get a clear MAP and draft clauses to review.

Best,
Samira
Senior Director, IT Security
ArborBio

[attachment: arbor_network_sketch.pdf (image/stub)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@arborbio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — KMS responsibilities & handoff questions

Samira — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in our Legal (Laura), Solutions (Monica), Ops (Marcus) and Privacy (Rishi) so we can respond with a single, actionable package.

Short answers up front:
- BYOK + customer-managed KMS: Yes. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for private deployments. Redwood will not persist plaintext master key material outside your KMS. We can integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS, and HSM appliances via standard KMIP where required.
- Operator access: We can adopt a model where operator tooling runs in your VPC via a restricted bastion/jump host (customer-hosted), with session recording and immutable audit logs shipped to your customer-owned log bucket. Our operators would only have access to de-identified logs unless breakglass is exercised under an approved, documented process.
- Subprocessors & telemetry: We'll provide a full subprocessors list and can configure telemetry to keep all sensitive artifacts inside your VPC. Any optional external monitoring (e.g., CloudForge agent) is configurable and documented in the MAP.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) Attached: Redwood draft — "redwood_private_dpa_draft_v1.pdf" (legal + private-deploy addendum).
2) Attached: MAP spreadsheet (MAP-ArborBio-20270418.xlsx) with proposed timeline, responsibilities, and action owners.
3) Ops to provide a short runbook for operator access and breakglass that you can review.

Can we schedule a 45-minute call this Thursday or next Tuesday to walk through the DPA redlines and the MAP? I'll send proposed times.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[attachments: redwood_private_dpa_draft_v1.pdf (application/pdf), MAP-ArborBio-20270418.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Carlos Diaz <legal@arborbio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@arborbio.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — KMS responsibilities & handoff questions

Ben / Laura — thanks for the quick response and the draft DPA. Our legal team reviewed and has three priority points (attached as redlines):

1) Key custody: ArborBio requires an explicit clause that Redwood will never possess or be able to reconstruct plaintext master keys. The clause should prohibit any outbound export of unencrypted key material and require monthly attestations for installations where Redwood performs maintenance.

2) Subprocessor enumeration & approval: Please provide a non-exhaustive list of potential subprocessors (monitoring, metrics, SRE tooling) and a commitment that any new subprocessor for this private deployment will require 30 days' notice and ArborBio approval for the next 12 months.

3) Cross-border transfer & retention: Clarify where backups, logs, and core model artifacts are stored and the controls preventing inadvertent transfer outside the US region. If any crash dumps or diagnostics are forwarded to Redwood or a third party, we require encryption-at-rest+in-flight and a 90-day retention maximum unless otherwise agreed.

We attached our annotated DPA (ArborBio_DPA_Redlines_20270428.docx). Also, please confirm you can sign a short amendment (SOW) that maps the MAP activities and acceptance criteria — we aim to finish contracting within two weeks after the DPA is agreed.

Regards,
Carlos Diaz
Counsel — ArborBio

[attachment: ArborBio_DPA_Redlines_20270428.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@arborbio.com>, Carlos Diaz <legal@arborbio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, CloudForge Integration <partner@cloudforge.io>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — KMS responsibilities & handoff questions

Carlos / Samira — appreciated. Laura and I reviewed ArborBio's redlines and Monica/Marcus drafted the ops runbook. High-level response and concrete next steps below: 

- Key custody: We will add the explicit prohibition on Redwood retaining or reconstructing plaintext master keys in the next DPA revision. We'll also include a monthly attestation schedule for maintenance windows where Redwood needs temporary access to support tooling; the attestation will log scope and duration.

- Subprocessors: Attached is an initial list of subprocessors used in Private deployments (monitoring agents, metrics pipelines, support tools). We'll add the 30-day notice + approval clause for material changes for the next 12 months.

- Cross-border & retention: All backups and core artifacts for your deployment can be configured to remain within the US region and into your customer-owned buckets. Crash dumps are by default stored only in-customer VPC; if you opt-in to support uploads they will be encrypted and retained for a maximum of 90 days unless you request longer.

Action items / timeline:
1) Redwood Legal (Laura) — finalize DPA v1.1 with the three changes above by Mon, 3 May 2027.
2) Ops (Marcus & Monica) — publish operator runbook and sample audit log within 48 hours of DPA v1.1.
3) ArborBio (Samira & Carlos) — review DPA v1.1 and MAP; provide final comments within 5 business days.
4) DocuSign link and SOW: I'll circulate the DocuSign envelope once DPA v1.1 is accepted; target signature by 12 May 2027.

Proposed call times for next week: Tue 04/05 09:30-10:15 PT or Wed 04/06 13:00-13:45 PT — happy to adjust.

Thanks — talk soon.
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
